108	def _parse_plan_entry(entry: dict[str, object]) -> "ExecutionPlan":
109	    """Validate one serialized plan record and rebuild the :class:`ExecutionPlan`."""
110	
111	    def pos_int(name: str) -> int:
112	        value = entry.get(name)
113	        _require(
114	            isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
115	            f"plan {entry.get('plan_id')!r} {name} must be a positive integer",
116	        )
117	        return value
118	
119	    plan_id = entry.get("plan_id")
120	    _require(_is_non_empty_str(plan_id), "plan plan_id must be a non-empty string")
121	    side = entry.get("side")
122	    _require(side in (BUY, SELL), f"plan {plan_id} has a bad side")
123	    order_type = entry.get("order_type")
124	    _require(order_type in (LIMIT, MARKET), f"plan {plan_id} has a bad order type")
125	    benchmark_price = pos_int("benchmark_price")
126	    price = entry.get("price")
127	    if order_type == LIMIT:
128	        _require(
129	            isinstance(price, int) and not isinstance(price, bool) and price > 0,
130	            f"plan {plan_id} LIMIT price must be a positive integer",
131	        )
132	    else:
133	        _require(price is None, f"plan {plan_id} MARKET must not carry a price")
134	    account_id = entry.get("account_id")
135	    _require(
136	        account_id is None or _is_non_empty_str(account_id),
137	        f"plan {plan_id} account_id is malformed",
138	    )
139	    raw_slices = entry.get("slice_quantities")
140	    _require(isinstance(raw_slices, list), f"plan {plan_id} slice_quantities must be a list")
141	    slice_quantities: list[int] = []
142	    for value in raw_slices:
143	        _require(
144	            isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
145	            f"plan {plan_id} slice quantities must be positive integers",
146	        )
147	        slice_quantities.append(value)
148	    released = entry.get("released")
149	    released_quantity = entry.get("released_quantity")
150	    filled_quantity = entry.get("filled_quantity")
151	    cancelled_quantity = entry.get("cancelled_quantity")
152	    notional = entry.get("notional")
153	    for name, value in (
154	        ("released", released),
155	        ("released_quantity", released_quantity),
156	        ("filled_quantity", filled_quantity),
157	        ("cancelled_quantity", cancelled_quantity),
158	        ("notional", notional),
159	    ):
160	        _require(_non_negative_int(value), f"plan {plan_id} {name} must be a non-negative integer")
161	    status = entry.get("status")
162	    _require(
163	        status in (PLAN_ACTIVE, PLAN_COMPLETED, PLAN_CANCELLED),
164	        f"plan {plan_id} has a bad status",
165	    )
166	    algorithm = entry.get("algorithm", ALGORITHM_TWAP)
167	    volume_weights: list[int] | None = None
168	    participation_bps: int | None = None
169	    market_volume: int | None = None
170	    plan_total: int | None = None
171	
172	    slice_count = len(slice_quantities)
173	    _require(0 <= released <= slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} released slice index out of range")
174	
175	    if algorithm == ALGORITHM_VWAP:
176	        # TWAP/VWAP plans always carry at least one scheduled slice.
177	        _require(slice_count > 0, f"plan {plan_id} slice_quantities must be a non-empty list")
178	        total_quantity = sum(slice_quantities)
179	        raw_weights = entry.get("volume_weights")
180	        _require(
181	            isinstance(raw_weights, list) and len(raw_weights) == slice_count,
182	            f"plan {plan_id} volume_weights must be a list matching its slices",
183	        )
184	        volume_weights = []
185	        for value in raw_weights:
186	            _require(
187	                isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
188	                f"plan {plan_id} volume weights must be positive integers",
189	            )
190	            volume_weights.append(value)
191	        _require(
192	            slice_quantities == _allocate_slices(total_quantity, volume_weights),
193	            f"plan {plan_id} slice quantities disagree with its volume weights",
194	        )
195	        _require(
196	            released_quantity == sum(slice_quantities[:released]),
197	            f"plan {plan_id} released_quantity does not match its slices",
198	        )
199	    elif algorithm == ALGORITHM_POV:
200	        # POV carries an explicit total and rate; its slice list holds exactly
201	        # one original quantity per positive release and may be empty before
202	        # the first one.
203	        plan_total = pos_int("total_quantity")
204	        participation_bps = entry.get("participation_bps")
205	        _require(
206	            _is_int(participation_bps) and 1 <= participation_bps <= 10000,
207	            f"plan {plan_id} participation_bps must be an integer from 1 to 10000",
208	        )
209	        market_volume = entry.get("market_volume")
210	        _require(
211	            _non_negative_int(market_volume),
212	            f"plan {plan_id} market_volume must be a non-negative integer",
213	        )
214	        _require(
215	            released == slice_count,
216	            f"plan {plan_id} POV release count disagrees with its released slices",
217	        )
218	        _require(
219	            released_quantity == sum(slice_quantities),
220	            f"plan {plan_id} released_quantity does not match its releases",
221	        )
222	        _require(
223	            released_quantity <= plan_total,
224	            f"plan {plan_id} released quantity exceeds its total",
225	        )
226	        # Every accepted POV_VOLUME event leaves the released quantity exactly
227	        # at the participation target for the cumulative market volume (capped
228	        # at the total), whatever lifecycle status followed.
229	        target = min(
230	            plan_total, market_volume * participation_bps // 10000
231	        )
232	        _require(
233	            released_quantity == target,
234	            f"plan {plan_id} released quantity disagrees with market volume",
235	        )
236	        total_quantity = plan_total
237	    else:
238	        _require(
239	            algorithm == ALGORITHM_TWAP,
240	            f"plan {plan_id} has an unknown algorithm",
241	        )
242	        _require(slice_count > 0, f"plan {plan_id} slice_quantities must be a non-empty list")
243	        total_quantity = sum(slice_quantities)
244	        _require(
245	            released_quantity == sum(slice_quantities[:released]),
246	            f"plan {plan_id} released_quantity does not match its slices",
247	        )
248	
249	    _require(
250	        filled_quantity <= released_quantity,
251	        f"plan {plan_id} filled quantity exceeds released quantity",
252	    )
253	
254	    if algorithm == ALGORITHM_POV:
255	        if status == PLAN_ACTIVE:
256	            _require(
257	                released_quantity < total_quantity,
258	                f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE after its total was released",
259	            )
260	            _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE but carries cancellations")
261	        elif status == PLAN_COMPLETED:
262	            _require(
263	                released_quantity == total_quantity,
264	                f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED before its total was released",
265	            )
266	            _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED but carries cancellations")
267	        else:
268	            _require(
269	                released_quantity < total_quantity,
270	                f"plan {plan_id} is CANCELLED after its total was released",
271	            )
272	            _require(
273	                cancelled_quantity == total_quantity - released_quantity,
274	                f"plan {plan_id} cancelled quantity does not cover the unreleased remainder",
275	            )
276	    elif status == PLAN_ACTIVE:
277	        _require(released < slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE with no slices left")
278	        _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE but carries cancellations")
279	    elif status == PLAN_COMPLETED:
280	        _require(released == slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED before all slices")
281	        _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED but carries cancellations")
282	    else:
283	        _require(released < slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} is CANCELLED after all slices")
284	        _require(
285	            cancelled_quantity == total_quantity - released_quantity,
286	            f"plan {plan_id} cancelled quantity does not cover the unreleased remainder",
287	        )
288	
289	    plan = ExecutionPlan.__new__(ExecutionPlan)
290	    plan.plan_id = plan_id
291	    plan.side = side
292	    plan.order_type = order_type
293	    plan.benchmark_price = benchmark_price
294	    plan.price = price
295	    plan.account_id = account_id
296	    plan.algorithm = algorithm
297	    plan.volume_weights = volume_weights
298	    plan.slice_quantities = slice_quantities
299	    plan.released = released
300	    plan.released_quantity = released_quantity
301	    plan.filled_quantity = filled_quantity
302	    plan.cancelled_quantity = cancelled_quantity
303	    plan.notional = notional
304	    plan.status = status
305	    plan.participation_bps = participation_bps
306	    plan.market_volume = market_volume
307	    plan.plan_total = plan_total
308	    return plan

345	def _engine_from_json(
346	    data: dict[str, object],
347	    config_price_limits: tuple[int, int] | None,
348	) -> _SymbolState:
349	    _require(isinstance(data, dict), "symbol state must be an object")
350	    keys = set(data)
351	    _require(
352	        keys == _SYMBOL_STATE_KEYS or keys == _SYMBOL_STATE_KEYS_LEGACY,
353	        "symbol state has unknown fields",
354	    )
355	    if "price_limits" in keys:
356	        raw_limits = data.get("price_limits")
357	        if raw_limits is None:
358	            price_limits: tuple[int, int] | None = None
359	        else:
360	            _require(
361	                isinstance(raw_limits, dict) and set(raw_limits) == {"lower", "upper"},
362	                "price_limits must be null or an object with exactly 'lower' and 'upper'",
363	            )
364	            lower = raw_limits["lower"]
365	            upper = raw_limits["upper"]
366	            _require(
367	                _is_positive_int(lower) and _is_positive_int(upper),
368	                "price_limits bounds must be positive integers",
369	            )
370	            _require(lower <= upper, "price_limits require lower <= upper")
371	            price_limits = (lower, upper)
372	    else:
373	        # A legacy snapshot predates intraday adjustments: the security had
374	        # only its static configured interval, so seed from the config.
375	        price_limits = config_price_limits
376	    last_sequence = data.get("last_sequence")
377	    _require(
378	        isinstance(last_sequence, int) and not isinstance(last_sequence, bool) and last_sequence >= 0,
379	        "last_sequence must be a non-negative integer",
380	    )
381	    event_log = data.get("event_log")
382	    _require(isinstance(event_log, list), "event_log must be a list")
383	    seen: dict[str, str] = {}
384	    for entry in event_log:
385	        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), "event_log entry must be an object")
386	        _require(set(entry) == {"event_id", "content"},
387	                 "event_log entry has unknown fields")
388	        event_id = entry.get("event_id")
389	        content = entry.get("content")
390	        _require(isinstance(event_id, str) and isinstance(content, str),
391	                 "event_log entry fields have wrong types")
392	        _require(event_id not in seen, "duplicate event id in symbol event log")
393	        seen[event_id] = content
394	
395	    # Partition the accepted events into baseline engine events and
396	    # replay-only events: the engine journal only knows the former plus the
397	    # child orders synthesized for released slices, while every TWAP/VWAP/POV
398	    # command id, every read-only EXECUTION_REPORT / IMPACT_REPORT id and
399	    # every PORTFOLIO_REPORT / PORTFOLIO_STRESS_REPORT id lives solely in the
400	    # replay log.
401	    baseline_event_ids: set[str] = set()
402	    replay_only_event_ids: set[str] = set()
403	    for event_id, content in seen.items():
404	        try:
405	            stored_type = json.loads(content).get("type")
406	        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
407	            _require(False, f"event log content for {event_id} is not a JSON object")
408	            stored_type = None
409	        if stored_type in _REPLAY_ONLY_TYPES:
410	            replay_only_event_ids.add(event_id)
411	        else:
412	            baseline_event_ids.add(event_id)
413	
414	    plans_raw = data.get("plans")
415	    _require(isinstance(plans_raw, list), "plans must be a list")
416	    plans: dict[str, ExecutionPlan] = {}
417	    plan_index: dict[str, str] = {}
418	    released_child_ids: set[str] = set()
419	    reserved_child_ids: set[str] = set()
420	    for entry in plans_raw:
421	        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), "plan entry must be an object")
422	        _require(
423	            set(entry) == _PLAN_KEYS
424	            or set(entry) == _VWAP_PLAN_KEYS
425	            or set(entry) == _POV_PLAN_KEYS,
426	            "plan entry has unknown fields",
427	        )
428	        plan = _parse_plan_entry(entry)
429	        plan_id = plan.plan_id
430	        _require(plan_id not in plans, f"duplicate execution plan id {plan_id}")
431	        for index in range(plan.child_count):
432	            child_id = plan.child_order_id(index + 1)
433	            _require(
434	                child_id not in plan_index,
435	                f"derived order id {child_id} is claimed by two plans",
436	            )
437	            plan_index[child_id] = plan_id
438	            if index < plan.released:
439	                released_child_ids.add(child_id)
440	            else:
441	                reserved_child_ids.add(child_id)
442	        plans[plan_id] = plan
443	
444	    engine_data = data.get("engine")
445	    _require(isinstance(engine_data, dict), "engine state must be an object")
446	    _require(set(engine_data) == _ENGINE_KEYS, "engine state has unknown fields")
447	
448	    event_ids = engine_data.get("event_ids")
449	    order_ids = engine_data.get("order_ids")
450	    reserved_raw = engine_data.get("reserved_order_ids")
451	    accounts = engine_data.get("accounts")
452	    _require(_is_str_set_list(event_ids), "engine.event_ids must be a list of strings")
453	    _require(_is_str_set_list(order_ids), "engine.order_ids must be a list of strings")
454	    _require(
455	        _is_str_set_list(reserved_raw),
456	        "engine.reserved_order_ids must be a list of strings",
457	    )
458	    _require(_is_str_set_list(accounts), "engine.accounts must be a list of strings")
459	    _require(
460	        set(reserved_raw) == reserved_child_ids,
461	        "reserved order ids do not match the plans' unreleased slices",
462	    )
463	    _require(
464	        set(reserved_raw).isdisjoint(order_ids),
465	        "an order id is both reserved and spent",
466	    )
467	
468	    orders = engine_data.get("orders")
469	    _require(isinstance(orders, dict), "engine.orders must be an object")
470	    for order_id, record in orders.items():
471	        _require(isinstance(order_id, str) and isinstance(record, dict),
472	                 "engine.orders entries are malformed")

474	                 f"order {order_id} has unknown fields")
475	
476	    def parse_levels(raw_levels: object, raw_totals: object, side_name: str):
477	        _require(isinstance(raw_levels, list), f"{side_name} levels must be a list")
478	        levels: list[tuple[int, list[str]]] = []
479	        seen_prices: set[int] = set()
480	        for level in raw_levels:
481	            _require(isinstance(level, dict), f"{side_name} level must be an object")
482	            _require(set(level) == {"price", "order_ids"},
483	                     f"{side_name} level has unknown fields")
484	            price = level.get("price")
485	            ids = level.get("order_ids")
486	            _require(
487	                isinstance(price, int) and not isinstance(price, bool) and price > 0,
488	                f"{side_name} level price must be a positive integer",
489	            )
490	            _require(_is_str_set_list(ids), f"{side_name} level order_ids must be strings")
491	            _require(price not in seen_prices, f"duplicate {side_name} price level")
492	            seen_prices.add(price)
493	            levels.append((price, ids))
494	        _require(isinstance(raw_totals, dict), f"{side_name} totals must be an object")
495	        totals: dict[int, int] = {}
496	        for price_text, qty in raw_totals.items():
497	            _require(isinstance(price_text, str), f"{side_name} total price key must be a string")
498	            try:
499	                price = int(price_text)
500	            except ValueError:
501	                _require(False, f"{side_name} total price key is not numeric")
502	            _require(str(price) == price_text and price > 0,
503	                     f"{side_name} total price key is not normalized")
504	            _require(isinstance(qty, int) and not isinstance(qty, bool) and qty > 0,
505	                     f"{side_name} total quantity must be a positive integer")
506	            totals[price] = qty
507	        _require(set(totals) == seen_prices,
508	                 f"{side_name} levels and aggregates disagree")
509	        return levels, totals
510	
511	    bid_levels, bid_totals = parse_levels(
512	        engine_data.get("bids"), engine_data.get("bid_totals"), "bid"
513	    )
514	    ask_levels, ask_totals = parse_levels(
515	        engine_data.get("asks"), engine_data.get("ask_totals"), "ask"
516	    )
517	
518	    bids = {price: deque(ids) for price, ids in bid_levels}
519	    asks = {price: deque(ids) for price, ids in ask_levels}
520	
521	    valid_status = {"FILLED", "RESTING", "CANCELLED"}
522	    for order_id, record in orders.items():
523	        side = record.get("side")
524	        status = record.get("status")
525	        remaining = record.get("remaining")
526	        price = record.get("price")
527	        _require(side in ("BUY", "SELL"), f"order {order_id} has a bad side")
528	        _require(status in valid_status, f"order {order_id} has a bad status")
529	        _require(
530	            isinstance(remaining, int) and not isinstance(remaining, bool) and remaining >= 0,
531	            f"order {order_id} remaining must be a non-negative integer",
532	        )
533	        _require(
534	            price is None or (isinstance(price, int) and not isinstance(price, bool) and price > 0),
535	            f"order {order_id} price is malformed",
536	        )
537	        if "account_id" in record:
538	            _require(isinstance(record["account_id"], str) and record["account_id"] != "",
539	                     f"order {order_id} account_id is malformed")
540	        if "display_quantity" in record or "visible" in record:
541	            # Iceberg records keep their peak size after they finish; a fully
542	            # filled record additionally carries a zero current slice, while a
543	            # cancelled one keeps the slice it had when removed.
544	            display_quantity = record.get("display_quantity")
545	            visible = record.get("visible")
546	            _require(
547	                isinstance(display_quantity, int) and not isinstance(display_quantity, bool)
548	                and display_quantity > 0,
549	                f"iceberg order {order_id} display_quantity is malformed",
550	            )
551	            _require(
552	                isinstance(visible, int) and not isinstance(visible, bool) and visible >= 0,
553	                f"iceberg order {order_id} visible slice is malformed",
554	            )
555	            if status == "RESTING":
556	                _require(visible > 0, f"resting iceberg {order_id} has no visible slice")
557	                _require(remaining > 0, f"resting iceberg {order_id} has no remainder")
558	                # The current slice may itself be partially consumed; it is only
559	                # reset to min(peak, remaining) once fully exhausted.
560	                _require(

563	                )
564	        else:

567	                f"resting order {order_id} must have a positive remainder",
568	            )
569	
570	    def check_level_aggregates(levels, totals, side_name):
571	        queued: set[str] = set()
572	        for price, ids in levels:
573	            level_visible = 0
574	            for order_id in ids:
575	                _require(order_id not in queued, f"order {order_id} queued twice")
576	                queued.add(order_id)
577	                record = orders.get(order_id)
578	                _require(record is not None, f"{side_name} queue references unknown order")
579	                level_visible += record.get("visible", record["remaining"])
580	            _require(level_visible == totals[price],
581	                     f"{side_name} aggregate at {price} does not match the queue")
582	        return queued
583	
584	    bid_queued = check_level_aggregates(bid_levels, bid_totals, "bid")
585	    ask_queued = check_level_aggregates(ask_levels, ask_totals, "ask")
586	    _require(bid_queued.isdisjoint(ask_queued), "an order rests on both sides")
587	
588	    # Every resting order is queued, and every finished order is not.
589	    resting = {oid for oid, rec in orders.items() if rec["status"] == "RESTING"}
590	    _require(resting == bid_queued | ask_queued,
591	             "resting orders and queued orders disagree")
592	    for order_id in bid_queued:
593	        _require(orders[order_id]["side"] == "BUY", f"{order_id} rests on the wrong side")
594	    for order_id in ask_queued:
595	        _require(orders[order_id]["side"] == "SELL", f"{order_id} rests on the wrong side")
596	
597	    # The id sets mirror exactly what the baseline engine would hold. The
598	    # engine only knows baseline events and synthesized child orders;
599	    # TWAP/VWAP/POV command ids live solely in the replay layer's event log.
600	    _require(set(order_ids) == set(orders), "order_ids and order records disagree")
601	    _require(
602	        set(event_ids) == (baseline_event_ids - set(plan_index)) | released_child_ids,
603	        "engine event ids do not match the baseline events and released slices",
604	    )
605	    _require(
606	        released_child_ids <= set(order_ids),
607	        "a released plan slice is missing an engine order record",
608	    )
609	    _require(
610	        released_child_ids.isdisjoint(reserved_child_ids),
611	        "a plan slice is both released and reserved",
612	    )
613	    _require(last_sequence == len(seen),
614	             "last_sequence does not match the contiguous accepted event count")
615	
616	    for record in orders.values():
617	        account_id = record.get("account_id")
618	        if account_id is not None:
619	            _require(account_id in accounts, f"account {account_id} missing from accounts")
620	
621	    next_trade_id = engine_data.get("next_trade_id")
622	    _require(
623	        isinstance(next_trade_id, int) and not isinstance(next_trade_id, bool) and next_trade_id >= 1,
624	        "next_trade_id must be a positive integer",
625	    )
626	
627	    trade_log = engine_data.get("trade_log")
628	    _require(isinstance(trade_log, list), "trade_log must be a list")
629	    expected_trade_id = 1
630	    for trade in trade_log:
631	        _require(isinstance(trade, dict), "trade log entry must be an object")
632	        _require(set(trade) == _TRADE_KEYS, "trade log entry has unknown fields")
633	        trade_id = trade.get("trade_id")
634	        _require(
635	            isinstance(trade_id, int) and not isinstance(trade_id, bool) and trade_id == expected_trade_id,
636	            "trade log ids must be consecutive from 1",
637	        )
638	        expected_trade_id += 1
639	        for key in ("maker_order_id", "taker_order_id", "event_id"):
640	            _require(isinstance(trade.get(key), str), f"trade log {key} must be a string")
641	        for key in ("price", "quantity"):
642	            value = trade.get(key)
643	            _require(
644	                isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
645	                f"trade log {key} must be a positive integer",
646	            )
647	    _require(next_trade_id == expected_trade_id,
648	             "next_trade_id does not match the cumulative trade log")
649	
650	    # Historical trades may only reference orders and events that the engine
651	    # still considers accepted.
652	    for trade in trade_log:
653	        maker_id = trade["maker_order_id"]
654	        taker_id = trade["taker_order_id"]
655	        trade_event_id = trade["event_id"]
656	        _require(maker_id in orders, f"trade references unknown maker {maker_id}")
657	        _require(taker_id in orders, f"trade references unknown taker {taker_id}")
658	        _require(trade_event_id in event_ids,
659	                 f"trade references unknown event {trade_event_id}")
660	        maker = orders[maker_id]
661	        taker = orders[taker_id]
662	        _require(maker["side"] != taker["side"], "a trade cannot join two same-side orders")
663	
664	    # Cross-validate every plan against the engine journal and order records:
665	    # released child ids must denote IOC child orders with the plan's side and
666	    # account, the child's original quantity must equal its slice quantity, and
667	    # the cumulative filled quantity / notional must match the trades exactly.
668	    child_fill_qty: dict[str, int] = {}
669	    child_notional: dict[str, int] = {}
670	    for trade in trade_log:
671	        taker_id = trade["taker_order_id"]
672	        if taker_id in plan_index:
673	            child_fill_qty[taker_id] = child_fill_qty.get(taker_id, 0) + trade["quantity"]
674	            child_notional[taker_id] = (
675	                child_notional.get(taker_id, 0) + trade["price"] * trade["quantity"]
676	            )
677	    for plan in plans.values():
678	        plan_filled = 0
679	        plan_notional = 0
680	        for index in range(plan.slice_count):
681	            child_id = plan.child_order_id(index + 1)
682	            if index >= plan.released:
683	                _require(
684	                    child_id not in orders,
685	                    f"plan {plan.plan_id} unreleased slice already has an order record",
686	                )
687	                continue
688	            record = orders[child_id]
689	            _require(record["side"] == plan.side,
690	                     f"child {child_id} trades on the wrong side")
691	            _require(record["status"] != "RESTING",
692	                     f"IOC child {child_id} must not rest in the book")
693	            _require(
694	                record["price"] == plan.price,
695	                f"child {child_id} price disagrees with its plan",
696	            )
697	            _require(
698	                record.get("account_id") == plan.account_id,
699	                f"child {child_id} account disagrees with its plan",
700	            )
701	            filled = child_fill_qty.get(child_id, 0)
702	            slice_quantity = plan.slice_quantities[index]
703	            _require(
704	                filled + record["remaining"] == slice_quantity,
705	                f"child {child_id} quantity does not match its plan slice",
706	            )
707	            plan_filled += filled
708	            plan_notional += child_notional.get(child_id, 0)
709	        _require(plan_filled == plan.filled_quantity,
710	                 f"plan {plan.plan_id} filled quantity disagrees with the trade log")

712	                 f"plan {plan.plan_id} notional disagrees with the trade log")
713	
714	    # Every derived id is either a released child order or an engine
715	    # reservation; no plan id may be missing on either side, and external
716	    # orders may never squat on a derived id.
717	    _require(
718	        set(plan_index) == released_child_ids | reserved_child_ids,
719	        "plan derived ids disagree with engine order state",
720	    )
721	    _require(
722	        released_child_ids.isdisjoint(reserved_child_ids),
723	        "a plan slice is both released and reserved",
724	    )
725	
726	    # Deep copy so later caller mutation of the snapshot document can never
727	    # reach the live engine.
728	    engine = Engine(
729	        _state={
730	            "event_ids": set(event_ids),
731	            "order_ids": set(order_ids),
732	            "reserved_order_ids": set(reserved_raw),
733	            "orders": copy.deepcopy(orders),
734	            "bids": bids,
735	            "asks": asks,
736	            "bid_totals": bid_totals,
737	            "ask_totals": ask_totals,
738	            "next_trade_id": next_trade_id,
739	            "accounts": set(accounts),
740	            "trade_log": copy.deepcopy(trade_log),
741	        }

743	    state = _SymbolState(engine)
744	    state.last_sequence = last_sequence
745	    state.seen = seen
746	    state.plans = plans
747	    state.plan_index = plan_index
748	    state.price_limits = price_limits

751	
752	def dump_session(session: object) -> dict[str, object]:
753	    """Export a resumable, JSON-compatible snapshot of a replay session.
754	
755	    The snapshot fully preserves (per security): price-time queue priority,
756	    order remainders, the iceberg current slice and replenishment state, the
757	    last sequence, cumulative trades, the next trade id counter and the
758	    active price-limit interval. It also carries the format version, the
759	    matching configuration (plus its digest) and a SHA-256 digest over the
760	    normalized whole document.
761	    """
762	    symbols = [
763	        {"symbol": symbol, "state": _engine_to_json(session._symbols[symbol])}
764	        for symbol in sorted(session._symbols)
765	    ]
766	    content = {
767	        "symbols": symbols,
768	        "events": [
769	            {"event_id": event_id, "symbol": symbol, "content": content_str}
770	            for event_id, (symbol, content_str) in sorted(session._events.items())
771	        ],
772	    }
773	    envelope: dict[str, object] = {
774	        "format_version": FORMAT_VERSION,
775	        "engine_version": __version__,
776	        "config": session.config,
777	        "config_digest": session.config_digest,
778	        "content": content,
779	    }
780	    envelope["content_digest"] = _digest(
781	        {key: value for key, value in envelope.items() if key != "content_digest"}
782	    )
783	    return envelope
784	
785	
786	def parse_snapshot(
787	    snapshot: dict[str, object],
788	    config: dict[str, object] | None = None,
789	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], dict[str, _SymbolState], dict[str, tuple[str, str]]]:
790	    """Verify a snapshot document and return the restored session state.
791	
792	    Version, configuration digest and content SHA-256 are verified before any
793	    state is built, and the whole session is assembled in locals that the
794	    caller adopts only after a successful return. Any failure raises
795	    :class:`SnapshotError` and leaves no partially recovered state behind.
796	
797	    Returns ``(expected_config, symbols, events)``: the configuration the
798	    resumed session must run with, the per-security states and the global
799	    idempotency log.
800	    """
801	    if not isinstance(snapshot, dict):
802	        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot must be a JSON object")
803	    if not set(snapshot) <= _ENVELOPE_KEYS_SNAPSHOT:
804	        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot document has unknown fields")
805	
806	    # A malformed caller configuration is a request error and is rejected
807	    # before any snapshot content (or the configuration comparison) is
808	    # consulted, so it never masquerades as a CONFIG_MISMATCH.
809	    _validate_config(dict(DEFAULT_CONFIG if config is None else config))
810	
811	    version = snapshot.get("format_version")
812	    if version != FORMAT_VERSION:
813	        raise SnapshotError(
814	            SNAPSHOT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED,
815	            f"unsupported snapshot format version: {version!r}",
816	        )
817	    engine_version = snapshot.get("engine_version")
818	    if not isinstance(engine_version, str) or engine_version == "":
819	        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot engine_version is malformed")
820	
821	    expected_config = DEFAULT_CONFIG if config is None else config
822	    snapshot_config = snapshot.get("config")
823	    if snapshot_config != expected_config:
824	        raise SnapshotError(CONFIG_MISMATCH, "snapshot configuration does not match")
825	    if snapshot.get("config_digest") != _digest(expected_config):
826	        raise SnapshotError(CONFIG_MISMATCH, "snapshot configuration digest does not match")
827	
828	    stored_digest = snapshot.get("content_digest")
829	    actual_digest = _digest(
830	        {key: value for key, value in snapshot.items() if key != "content_digest"}
831	    )
832	    if not isinstance(stored_digest, str) or stored_digest != actual_digest:
833	        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot content digest mismatch")
834	
835	    content = snapshot.get("content")
836	    if (
837	        not isinstance(content, dict)
838	        or set(content) != _CONTENT_KEYS
839	        or not isinstance(content.get("symbols"), list)
840	        or not isinstance(content.get("events"), list)
841	    ):
842	        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot content is malformed")
843	
844	    # The resumed session runs with the caller's configuration; a non-object
845	    # configuration is a request error, exactly as the session constructor
846	    # would raise before any snapshot content is adopted.
847	    if not isinstance(expected_config, dict):
848	        raise TypeError("config must be a JSON object or None")
849	
850	    # Build the whole session in locals first; the caller commits it to the
851	    # session object only after every component parsed successfully.
852	    config_price_limits = {
853	        symbol: (bounds["lower"], bounds["upper"])
854	        for symbol, bounds in (expected_config.get("price_limits") or {}).items()
855	    }
856	    symbols: dict[str, _SymbolState] = {}
857	    events: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
858	    for entry in content["symbols"]:
859	        if not (
860	            isinstance(entry, dict)
861	            and set(entry) == {"symbol", "state"}
862	            and isinstance(entry.get("symbol"), str)
863	            and isinstance(entry.get("state"), dict)
864	        ):
865	            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot symbol entry is malformed")
866	        symbol = entry["symbol"]
867	        if symbol in symbols:
868	            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"duplicate symbol in snapshot: {symbol}")
869	        try:
870	            symbols[symbol] = _engine_from_json(
871	                entry["state"], config_price_limits.get(symbol)
872	            )
873	        except (KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
874	            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"snapshot state for {symbol} is malformed") from exc
875	    for entry in content.get("events", []):
876	        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"event_id", "symbol", "content"}:
877	            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot event log is malformed")
878	        event_id = entry.get("event_id")
879	        symbol = entry.get("symbol")
880	        text = entry.get("content")
881	        if not isinstance(event_id, str) or not isinstance(symbol, str) or not isinstance(text, str):
882	            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot event log entry is malformed")
883	        if symbol not in symbols:
884	            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"event {event_id} references unknown symbol")
885	        if event_id in events:
886	            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"duplicate event id in snapshot: {event_id}")
887	        events[event_id] = (symbol, text)
888	
889	    # The global event log and the per-symbol event logs must describe exactly
890	    # the same accepted events, with identical normalized content.
891	    logged_per_symbol: dict[str, int] = {}
892	    for symbol, text in events.values():
893	        logged_per_symbol[symbol] = logged_per_symbol.get(symbol, 0) + 1
894	    for symbol, symbol_state in symbols.items():
895	        for event_id, text in symbol_state.seen.items():
896	            if events.get(event_id) != (symbol, text):
897	                raise SnapshotError(
898	                    SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT,
899	                    f"event {event_id} disagrees between global and symbol log",
900	                )
901	        if logged_per_symbol.get(symbol, 0) != len(symbol_state.seen):
902	            raise SnapshotError(
903	                SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT,
904	                f"event log counts disagree for symbol {symbol}",
905	            )
906	
907	    return expected_config, symbols, events

"""Snapshot export and restoration: state persistence for replay sessions.

This module serializes a session's complete state (per-security order
queues, accounts, plans, active price-limit intervals, event logs, reserved
derived order ids and trade numbering) into a JSON-compatible document and
parses such a document back into plain state containers, verifying every
cross-invariant along the way. It never imports the orchestrator:
:func:`dump_session` reads any session with the standard state attributes
and :func:`parse_snapshot` returns the restored pieces for the caller to
install, so persistence and event orchestration stay decoupled. Any
verification failure raises :class:`SnapshotError` before any state is
adopted, so no partially recovered session is ever observable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json
from collections import deque

from .. import __version__
from ..engine import (
    BUY,
    LIMIT,
    MARKET,
    SELL,
    Engine,
    _is_int,
    _is_non_empty_str,
    _is_positive_int,
)
from .constants import (
    ALGORITHM_POV,
    ALGORITHM_TWAP,
    ALGORITHM_VWAP,
    CONFIG_MISMATCH,
    DEFAULT_CONFIG,
    FORMAT_VERSION,
    PLAN_ACTIVE,
    PLAN_CANCELLED,
    PLAN_COMPLETED,
    SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT,
    SNAPSHOT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED,
    _REPLAY_ONLY_TYPES,
)
from .errors import SnapshotError
from .plan import ExecutionPlan
from .serialization import _digest
from .state import _SymbolState
from .validation import _allocate_slices, _validate_config


def _engine_to_json(state: _SymbolState) -> dict[str, object]:
    raw = state.engine.dump_state()
    return {
        "last_sequence": state.last_sequence,
        # The security's active price-limit interval travels with the
        # snapshot so a resumed run enforces exactly the band a continuous
        # run would; ``None`` means the security is unlimited.
        "price_limits": (
            {"lower": state.price_limits[0], "upper": state.price_limits[1]}
            if state.price_limits is not None
            else None
        ),
        "event_log": [
            {"event_id": event_id, "content": content}
            for event_id, content in state.seen.items()
        ],
        "plans": [state.plans[plan_id].to_json() for plan_id in sorted(state.plans)],
        "engine": {
            "event_ids": sorted(raw["event_ids"]),
            "order_ids": sorted(raw["order_ids"]),
            "reserved_order_ids": sorted(raw["reserved_order_ids"]),
            "orders": {
                order_id: raw["orders"][order_id]
                for order_id in sorted(raw["orders"])
            },
            "bids": [
                {"price": price, "order_ids": list(queue)}
                for price, queue in sorted(raw["bids"].items())
            ],
            "asks": [
                {"price": price, "order_ids": list(queue)}
                for price, queue in sorted(raw["asks"].items())
            ],
            "bid_totals": {str(price): qty for price, qty in sorted(raw["bid_totals"].items())},
            "ask_totals": {str(price): qty for price, qty in sorted(raw["ask_totals"].items())},
            "next_trade_id": raw["next_trade_id"],
            "accounts": sorted(raw["accounts"]),
            "trade_log": raw["trade_log"],
        },
    }


def _require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, message)


def _is_str_set_list(value: object) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, list) and all(isinstance(item, str) for item in value)


def _non_negative_int(value: object) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0


def _parse_plan_entry(entry: dict[str, object]) -> "ExecutionPlan":
    """Validate one serialized plan record and rebuild the :class:`ExecutionPlan`."""

    def pos_int(name: str) -> int:
        value = entry.get(name)
        _require(
            isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
            f"plan {entry.get('plan_id')!r} {name} must be a positive integer",
        )
        return value

    plan_id = entry.get("plan_id")
    _require(_is_non_empty_str(plan_id), "plan plan_id must be a non-empty string")
    side = entry.get("side")
    _require(side in (BUY, SELL), f"plan {plan_id} has a bad side")
    order_type = entry.get("order_type")
    _require(order_type in (LIMIT, MARKET), f"plan {plan_id} has a bad order type")
    benchmark_price = pos_int("benchmark_price")
    price = entry.get("price")
    if order_type == LIMIT:
        _require(
            isinstance(price, int) and not isinstance(price, bool) and price > 0,
            f"plan {plan_id} LIMIT price must be a positive integer",
        )
    else:
        _require(price is None, f"plan {plan_id} MARKET must not carry a price")
    account_id = entry.get("account_id")
    _require(
        account_id is None or _is_non_empty_str(account_id),
        f"plan {plan_id} account_id is malformed",
    )
    raw_slices = entry.get("slice_quantities")
    _require(isinstance(raw_slices, list), f"plan {plan_id} slice_quantities must be a list")
    slice_quantities: list[int] = []
    for value in raw_slices:
        _require(
            isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
            f"plan {plan_id} slice quantities must be positive integers",
        )
        slice_quantities.append(value)
    released = entry.get("released")
    released_quantity = entry.get("released_quantity")
    filled_quantity = entry.get("filled_quantity")
    cancelled_quantity = entry.get("cancelled_quantity")
    notional = entry.get("notional")
    for name, value in (
        ("released", released),
        ("released_quantity", released_quantity),
        ("filled_quantity", filled_quantity),
        ("cancelled_quantity", cancelled_quantity),
        ("notional", notional),
    ):
        _require(_non_negative_int(value), f"plan {plan_id} {name} must be a non-negative integer")
    status = entry.get("status")
    _require(
        status in (PLAN_ACTIVE, PLAN_COMPLETED, PLAN_CANCELLED),
        f"plan {plan_id} has a bad status",
    )
    algorithm = entry.get("algorithm", ALGORITHM_TWAP)
    volume_weights: list[int] | None = None
    participation_bps: int | None = None
    market_volume: int | None = None
    plan_total: int | None = None

    slice_count = len(slice_quantities)
    _require(0 <= released <= slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} released slice index out of range")

    if algorithm == ALGORITHM_VWAP:
        # TWAP/VWAP plans always carry at least one scheduled slice.
        _require(slice_count > 0, f"plan {plan_id} slice_quantities must be a non-empty list")
        total_quantity = sum(slice_quantities)
        raw_weights = entry.get("volume_weights")
        _require(
            isinstance(raw_weights, list) and len(raw_weights) == slice_count,
            f"plan {plan_id} volume_weights must be a list matching its slices",
        )
        volume_weights = []
        for value in raw_weights:
            _require(
                isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
                f"plan {plan_id} volume weights must be positive integers",
            )
            volume_weights.append(value)
        _require(
            slice_quantities == _allocate_slices(total_quantity, volume_weights),
            f"plan {plan_id} slice quantities disagree with its volume weights",
        )
        _require(
            released_quantity == sum(slice_quantities[:released]),
            f"plan {plan_id} released_quantity does not match its slices",
        )
    elif algorithm == ALGORITHM_POV:
        # POV carries an explicit total and rate; its slice list holds exactly
        # one original quantity per positive release and may be empty before
        # the first one.
        plan_total = pos_int("total_quantity")
        participation_bps = entry.get("participation_bps")
        _require(
            _is_int(participation_bps) and 1 <= participation_bps <= 10000,
            f"plan {plan_id} participation_bps must be an integer from 1 to 10000",
        )
        market_volume = entry.get("market_volume")
        _require(
            _non_negative_int(market_volume),
            f"plan {plan_id} market_volume must be a non-negative integer",
        )
        _require(
            released == slice_count,
            f"plan {plan_id} POV release count disagrees with its released slices",
        )
        _require(
            released_quantity == sum(slice_quantities),
            f"plan {plan_id} released_quantity does not match its releases",
        )
        _require(
            released_quantity <= plan_total,
            f"plan {plan_id} released quantity exceeds its total",
        )
        # Every accepted POV_VOLUME event leaves the released quantity exactly
        # at the participation target for the cumulative market volume (capped
        # at the total), whatever lifecycle status followed.
        target = min(
            plan_total, market_volume * participation_bps // 10000
        )
        _require(
            released_quantity == target,
            f"plan {plan_id} released quantity disagrees with market volume",
        )
        total_quantity = plan_total
    else:
        _require(
            algorithm == ALGORITHM_TWAP,
            f"plan {plan_id} has an unknown algorithm",
        )
        _require(slice_count > 0, f"plan {plan_id} slice_quantities must be a non-empty list")
        total_quantity = sum(slice_quantities)
        _require(
            released_quantity == sum(slice_quantities[:released]),
            f"plan {plan_id} released_quantity does not match its slices",
        )

    _require(
        filled_quantity <= released_quantity,
        f"plan {plan_id} filled quantity exceeds released quantity",
    )

    if algorithm == ALGORITHM_POV:
        if status == PLAN_ACTIVE:
            _require(
                released_quantity < total_quantity,
                f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE after its total was released",
            )
            _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE but carries cancellations")
        elif status == PLAN_COMPLETED:
            _require(
                released_quantity == total_quantity,
                f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED before its total was released",
            )
            _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED but carries cancellations")
        else:
            _require(
                released_quantity < total_quantity,
                f"plan {plan_id} is CANCELLED after its total was released",
            )
            _require(
                cancelled_quantity == total_quantity - released_quantity,
                f"plan {plan_id} cancelled quantity does not cover the unreleased remainder",
            )
    elif status == PLAN_ACTIVE:
        _require(released < slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE with no slices left")
        _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE but carries cancellations")
    elif status == PLAN_COMPLETED:
        _require(released == slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED before all slices")
        _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED but carries cancellations")
    else:
        _require(released < slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} is CANCELLED after all slices")
        _require(
            cancelled_quantity == total_quantity - released_quantity,
            f"plan {plan_id} cancelled quantity does not cover the unreleased remainder",
        )

    plan = ExecutionPlan.__new__(ExecutionPlan)
    plan.plan_id = plan_id
    plan.side = side
    plan.order_type = order_type
    plan.benchmark_price = benchmark_price
    plan.price = price
    plan.account_id = account_id
    plan.algorithm = algorithm
    plan.volume_weights = volume_weights
    plan.slice_quantities = slice_quantities
    plan.released = released
    plan.released_quantity = released_quantity
    plan.filled_quantity = filled_quantity
    plan.cancelled_quantity = cancelled_quantity
    plan.notional = notional
    plan.status = status
    plan.participation_bps = participation_bps
    plan.market_volume = market_volume
    plan.plan_total = plan_total
    return plan


_ORDER_RECORD_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"side", "price", "remaining", "status", "account_id",
     "display_quantity", "visible"}
)
_TRADE_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"trade_id", "maker_order_id", "taker_order_id", "price", "quantity", "event_id"}
)
_SYMBOL_STATE_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"last_sequence", "price_limits", "event_log", "plans", "engine"}
)
#: Snapshots written before the intraday price-limit adjustment existed
#: carry no per-symbol ``price_limits``; on restore the active interval is
#: seeded from the static configuration instead.
_SYMBOL_STATE_KEYS_LEGACY = _SYMBOL_STATE_KEYS - {"price_limits"}
_ENGINE_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"event_ids", "order_ids", "reserved_order_ids", "orders", "bids", "asks",
     "bid_totals", "ask_totals", "next_trade_id", "accounts", "trade_log"}
)
_PLAN_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"plan_id", "side", "order_type", "benchmark_price", "price", "account_id",
     "slice_quantities", "released", "released_quantity", "filled_quantity",
     "cancelled_quantity", "notional", "status"}
)
_VWAP_PLAN_KEYS = _PLAN_KEYS | {"algorithm", "volume_weights"}
_POV_PLAN_KEYS = _PLAN_KEYS | {
    "algorithm", "total_quantity", "participation_bps", "market_volume"
}
_ENVELOPE_KEYS_SNAPSHOT = frozenset(
    {"format_version", "engine_version", "config", "config_digest",
     "content", "content_digest"}
)
_CONTENT_KEYS = frozenset({"symbols", "events"})


def _engine_from_json(
    data: dict[str, object],
    config_price_limits: tuple[int, int] | None,
) -> _SymbolState:
    _require(isinstance(data, dict), "symbol state must be an object")
    keys = set(data)
    _require(
        keys == _SYMBOL_STATE_KEYS or keys == _SYMBOL_STATE_KEYS_LEGACY,
        "symbol state has unknown fields",
    )
    if "price_limits" in keys:
        raw_limits = data.get("price_limits")
        if raw_limits is None:
            price_limits: tuple[int, int] | None = None
        else:
            _require(
                isinstance(raw_limits, dict) and set(raw_limits) == {"lower", "upper"},
                "price_limits must be null or an object with exactly 'lower' and 'upper'",
            )
            lower = raw_limits["lower"]
            upper = raw_limits["upper"]
            _require(
                _is_positive_int(lower) and _is_positive_int(upper),
                "price_limits bounds must be positive integers",
            )
            _require(lower <= upper, "price_limits require lower <= upper")
            price_limits = (lower, upper)
    else:
        # A legacy snapshot predates intraday adjustments: the security had
        # only its static configured interval, so seed from the config.
        price_limits = config_price_limits
    last_sequence = data.get("last_sequence")
    _require(
        isinstance(last_sequence, int) and not isinstance(last_sequence, bool) and last_sequence >= 0,
        "last_sequence must be a non-negative integer",
    )
    event_log = data.get("event_log")
    _require(isinstance(event_log, list), "event_log must be a list")
    seen: dict[str, str] = {}
    for entry in event_log:
        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), "event_log entry must be an object")
        _require(set(entry) == {"event_id", "content"},
                 "event_log entry has unknown fields")
        event_id = entry.get("event_id")
        content = entry.get("content")
        _require(isinstance(event_id, str) and isinstance(content, str),
                 "event_log entry fields have wrong types")
        _require(event_id not in seen, "duplicate event id in symbol event log")
        seen[event_id] = content

    # Partition the accepted events into baseline engine events and
    # replay-only events: the engine journal only knows the former plus the
    # child orders synthesized for released slices, while every TWAP/VWAP/POV
    # command id, every read-only EXECUTION_REPORT / IMPACT_REPORT id and
    # every PORTFOLIO_REPORT / PORTFOLIO_STRESS_REPORT id lives solely in the
    # replay log.
    baseline_event_ids: set[str] = set()
    replay_only_event_ids: set[str] = set()
    for event_id, content in seen.items():
        try:
            stored_type = json.loads(content).get("type")
        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
            _require(False, f"event log content for {event_id} is not a JSON object")
            stored_type = None
        if stored_type in _REPLAY_ONLY_TYPES:
            replay_only_event_ids.add(event_id)
        else:
            baseline_event_ids.add(event_id)

    plans_raw = data.get("plans")
    _require(isinstance(plans_raw, list), "plans must be a list")
    plans: dict[str, ExecutionPlan] = {}
    plan_index: dict[str, str] = {}
    released_child_ids: set[str] = set()
    reserved_child_ids: set[str] = set()
    for entry in plans_raw:
        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), "plan entry must be an object")
        _require(
            set(entry) == _PLAN_KEYS
            or set(entry) == _VWAP_PLAN_KEYS
            or set(entry) == _POV_PLAN_KEYS,
            "plan entry has unknown fields",
        )
        plan = _parse_plan_entry(entry)
        plan_id = plan.plan_id
        _require(plan_id not in plans, f"duplicate execution plan id {plan_id}")
        for index in range(plan.child_count):
            child_id = plan.child_order_id(index + 1)
            _require(
                child_id not in plan_index,
                f"derived order id {child_id} is claimed by two plans",
            )
            plan_index[child_id] = plan_id
            if index < plan.released:
                released_child_ids.add(child_id)
            else:
                reserved_child_ids.add(child_id)
        plans[plan_id] = plan

    engine_data = data.get("engine")
    _require(isinstance(engine_data, dict), "engine state must be an object")
    _require(set(engine_data) == _ENGINE_KEYS, "engine state has unknown fields")

    event_ids = engine_data.get("event_ids")
    order_ids = engine_data.get("order_ids")
    reserved_raw = engine_data.get("reserved_order_ids")
    accounts = engine_data.get("accounts")
    _require(_is_str_set_list(event_ids), "engine.event_ids must be a list of strings")
    _require(_is_str_set_list(order_ids), "engine.order_ids must be a list of strings")
    _require(
        _is_str_set_list(reserved_raw),
        "engine.reserved_order_ids must be a list of strings",
    )
    _require(_is_str_set_list(accounts), "engine.accounts must be a list of strings")
    _require(
        set(reserved_raw) == reserved_child_ids,
        "reserved order ids do not match the plans' unreleased slices",
    )
    _require(
        set(reserved_raw).isdisjoint(order_ids),
        "an order id is both reserved and spent",
    )

    orders = engine_data.get("orders")
    _require(isinstance(orders, dict), "engine.orders must be an object")
    for order_id, record in orders.items():
        _require(isinstance(order_id, str) and isinstance(record, dict),
                 "engine.orders entries are malformed")
        _require(set(record) <= _ORDER_RECORD_KEYS,
                 f"order {order_id} has unknown fields")

    def parse_levels(raw_levels: object, raw_totals: object, side_name: str):
        _require(isinstance(raw_levels, list), f"{side_name} levels must be a list")
        levels: list[tuple[int, list[str]]] = []
        seen_prices: set[int] = set()
        for level in raw_levels:
            _require(isinstance(level, dict), f"{side_name} level must be an object")
            _require(set(level) == {"price", "order_ids"},
                     f"{side_name} level has unknown fields")
            price = level.get("price")
            ids = level.get("order_ids")
            _require(
                isinstance(price, int) and not isinstance(price, bool) and price > 0,
                f"{side_name} level price must be a positive integer",
            )
            _require(_is_str_set_list(ids), f"{side_name} level order_ids must be strings")
            _require(price not in seen_prices, f"duplicate {side_name} price level")
            seen_prices.add(price)
            levels.append((price, ids))
        _require(isinstance(raw_totals, dict), f"{side_name} totals must be an object")
        totals: dict[int, int] = {}
        for price_text, qty in raw_totals.items():
            _require(isinstance(price_text, str), f"{side_name} total price key must be a string")
            try:
                price = int(price_text)
            except ValueError:
                _require(False, f"{side_name} total price key is not numeric")
            _require(str(price) == price_text and price > 0,
                     f"{side_name} total price key is not normalized")
            _require(isinstance(qty, int) and not isinstance(qty, bool) and qty > 0,
                     f"{side_name} total quantity must be a positive integer")
            totals[price] = qty
        _require(set(totals) == seen_prices,
                 f"{side_name} levels and aggregates disagree")
        return levels, totals

    bid_levels, bid_totals = parse_levels(
        engine_data.get("bids"), engine_data.get("bid_totals"), "bid"
    )
    ask_levels, ask_totals = parse_levels(
        engine_data.get("asks"), engine_data.get("ask_totals"), "ask"
    )

    bids = {price: deque(ids) for price, ids in bid_levels}
    asks = {price: deque(ids) for price, ids in ask_levels}

    valid_status = {"FILLED", "RESTING", "CANCELLED"}
    for order_id, record in orders.items():
        side = record.get("side")
        status = record.get("status")
        remaining = record.get("remaining")
        price = record.get("price")
        _require(side in ("BUY", "SELL"), f"order {order_id} has a bad side")
        _require(status in valid_status, f"order {order_id} has a bad status")
        _require(
            isinstance(remaining, int) and not isinstance(remaining, bool) and remaining >= 0,
            f"order {order_id} remaining must be a non-negative integer",
        )
        _require(
            price is None or (isinstance(price, int) and not isinstance(price, bool) and price > 0),
            f"order {order_id} price is malformed",
        )
        if "account_id" in record:
            _require(isinstance(record["account_id"], str) and record["account_id"] != "",
                     f"order {order_id} account_id is malformed")
        if "display_quantity" in record or "visible" in record:
            # Iceberg records keep their peak size after they finish; a fully
            # filled record additionally carries a zero current slice, while a
            # cancelled one keeps the slice it had when removed.
            display_quantity = record.get("display_quantity")
            visible = record.get("visible")
            _require(
                isinstance(display_quantity, int) and not isinstance(display_quantity, bool)
                and display_quantity > 0,
                f"iceberg order {order_id} display_quantity is malformed",
            )
            _require(
                isinstance(visible, int) and not isinstance(visible, bool) and visible >= 0,
                f"iceberg order {order_id} visible slice is malformed",
            )
            if status == "RESTING":
                _require(visible > 0, f"resting iceberg {order_id} has no visible slice")
                _require(remaining > 0, f"resting iceberg {order_id} has no remainder")
                # The current slice may itself be partially consumed; it is only
                # reset to min(peak, remaining) once fully exhausted.
                _require(
                    visible <= min(display_quantity, remaining),
                    f"resting iceberg {order_id} slice exceeds peak or remainder",
                )
        else:
            _require(
                status != "RESTING" or remaining > 0,
                f"resting order {order_id} must have a positive remainder",
            )

    def check_level_aggregates(levels, totals, side_name):
        queued: set[str] = set()
        for price, ids in levels:
            level_visible = 0
            for order_id in ids:
                _require(order_id not in queued, f"order {order_id} queued twice")
                queued.add(order_id)
                record = orders.get(order_id)
                _require(record is not None, f"{side_name} queue references unknown order")
                level_visible += record.get("visible", record["remaining"])
            _require(level_visible == totals[price],
                     f"{side_name} aggregate at {price} does not match the queue")
        return queued

    bid_queued = check_level_aggregates(bid_levels, bid_totals, "bid")
    ask_queued = check_level_aggregates(ask_levels, ask_totals, "ask")
    _require(bid_queued.isdisjoint(ask_queued), "an order rests on both sides")

    # Every resting order is queued, and every finished order is not.
    resting = {oid for oid, rec in orders.items() if rec["status"] == "RESTING"}
    _require(resting == bid_queued | ask_queued,
             "resting orders and queued orders disagree")
    for order_id in bid_queued:
        _require(orders[order_id]["side"] == "BUY", f"{order_id} rests on the wrong side")
    for order_id in ask_queued:
        _require(orders[order_id]["side"] == "SELL", f"{order_id} rests on the wrong side")

    # The id sets mirror exactly what the baseline engine would hold. The
    # engine only knows baseline events and synthesized child orders;
    # TWAP/VWAP/POV command ids live solely in the replay layer's event log.
    _require(set(order_ids) == set(orders), "order_ids and order records disagree")
    _require(
        set(event_ids) == (baseline_event_ids - set(plan_index)) | released_child_ids,
        "engine event ids do not match the baseline events and released slices",
    )
    _require(
        released_child_ids <= set(order_ids),
        "a released plan slice is missing an engine order record",
    )
    _require(
        released_child_ids.isdisjoint(reserved_child_ids),
        "a plan slice is both released and reserved",
    )
    _require(last_sequence == len(seen),
             "last_sequence does not match the contiguous accepted event count")

    for record in orders.values():
        account_id = record.get("account_id")
        if account_id is not None:
            _require(account_id in accounts, f"account {account_id} missing from accounts")

    next_trade_id = engine_data.get("next_trade_id")
    _require(
        isinstance(next_trade_id, int) and not isinstance(next_trade_id, bool) and next_trade_id >= 1,
        "next_trade_id must be a positive integer",
    )

    trade_log = engine_data.get("trade_log")
    _require(isinstance(trade_log, list), "trade_log must be a list")
    expected_trade_id = 1
    for trade in trade_log:
        _require(isinstance(trade, dict), "trade log entry must be an object")
        _require(set(trade) == _TRADE_KEYS, "trade log entry has unknown fields")
        trade_id = trade.get("trade_id")
        _require(
            isinstance(trade_id, int) and not isinstance(trade_id, bool) and trade_id == expected_trade_id,
            "trade log ids must be consecutive from 1",
        )
        expected_trade_id += 1
        for key in ("maker_order_id", "taker_order_id", "event_id"):
            _require(isinstance(trade.get(key), str), f"trade log {key} must be a string")
        for key in ("price", "quantity"):
            value = trade.get(key)
            _require(
                isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
                f"trade log {key} must be a positive integer",
            )
    _require(next_trade_id == expected_trade_id,
             "next_trade_id does not match the cumulative trade log")

    # Historical trades may only reference orders and events that the engine
    # still considers accepted.
    for trade in trade_log:
        maker_id = trade["maker_order_id"]
        taker_id = trade["taker_order_id"]
        trade_event_id = trade["event_id"]
        _require(maker_id in orders, f"trade references unknown maker {maker_id}")
        _require(taker_id in orders, f"trade references unknown taker {taker_id}")
        _require(trade_event_id in event_ids,
                 f"trade references unknown event {trade_event_id}")
        maker = orders[maker_id]
        taker = orders[taker_id]
        _require(maker["side"] != taker["side"], "a trade cannot join two same-side orders")

    # Cross-validate every plan against the engine journal and order records:
    # released child ids must denote IOC child orders with the plan's side and
    # account, the child's original quantity must equal its slice quantity, and
    # the cumulative filled quantity / notional must match the trades exactly.
    child_fill_qty: dict[str, int] = {}
    child_notional: dict[str, int] = {}
    for trade in trade_log:
        taker_id = trade["taker_order_id"]
        if taker_id in plan_index:
            child_fill_qty[taker_id] = child_fill_qty.get(taker_id, 0) + trade["quantity"]
            child_notional[taker_id] = (
                child_notional.get(taker_id, 0) + trade["price"] * trade["quantity"]
            )
    for plan in plans.values():
        plan_filled = 0
        plan_notional = 0
        for index in range(plan.slice_count):
            child_id = plan.child_order_id(index + 1)
            if index >= plan.released:
                _require(
                    child_id not in orders,
                    f"plan {plan.plan_id} unreleased slice already has an order record",
                )
                continue
            record = orders[child_id]
            _require(record["side"] == plan.side,
                     f"child {child_id} trades on the wrong side")
            _require(record["status"] != "RESTING",
                     f"IOC child {child_id} must not rest in the book")
            _require(
                record["price"] == plan.price,
                f"child {child_id} price disagrees with its plan",
            )
            _require(
                record.get("account_id") == plan.account_id,
                f"child {child_id} account disagrees with its plan",
            )
            filled = child_fill_qty.get(child_id, 0)
            slice_quantity = plan.slice_quantities[index]
            _require(
                filled + record["remaining"] == slice_quantity,
                f"child {child_id} quantity does not match its plan slice",
            )
            plan_filled += filled
            plan_notional += child_notional.get(child_id, 0)
        _require(plan_filled == plan.filled_quantity,
                 f"plan {plan.plan_id} filled quantity disagrees with the trade log")
        _require(plan_notional == plan.notional,
                 f"plan {plan.plan_id} notional disagrees with the trade log")

    # Every derived id is either a released child order or an engine
    # reservation; no plan id may be missing on either side, and external
    # orders may never squat on a derived id.
    _require(
        set(plan_index) == released_child_ids | reserved_child_ids,
        "plan derived ids disagree with engine order state",
    )
    _require(
        released_child_ids.isdisjoint(reserved_child_ids),
        "a plan slice is both released and reserved",
    )

    # Deep copy so later caller mutation of the snapshot document can never
    # reach the live engine.
    engine = Engine(
        _state={
            "event_ids": set(event_ids),
            "order_ids": set(order_ids),
            "reserved_order_ids": set(reserved_raw),
            "orders": copy.deepcopy(orders),
            "bids": bids,
            "asks": asks,
            "bid_totals": bid_totals,
            "ask_totals": ask_totals,
            "next_trade_id": next_trade_id,
            "accounts": set(accounts),
            "trade_log": copy.deepcopy(trade_log),
        }
    )
    state = _SymbolState(engine)
    state.last_sequence = last_sequence
    state.seen = seen
    state.plans = plans
    state.plan_index = plan_index
    state.price_limits = price_limits
    return state


def dump_session(session: object) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Export a resumable, JSON-compatible snapshot of a replay session.

    The snapshot fully preserves (per security): price-time queue priority,
    order remainders, the iceberg current slice and replenishment state, the
    last sequence, cumulative trades, the next trade id counter and the
    active price-limit interval. It also carries the format version, the
    matching configuration (plus its digest) and a SHA-256 digest over the
    normalized whole document.
    """
    symbols = [
        {"symbol": symbol, "state": _engine_to_json(session._symbols[symbol])}
        for symbol in sorted(session._symbols)
    ]
    content = {
        "symbols": symbols,
        "events": [
            {"event_id": event_id, "symbol": symbol, "content": content_str}
            for event_id, (symbol, content_str) in sorted(session._events.items())
        ],
    }
    envelope: dict[str, object] = {
        "format_version": FORMAT_VERSION,
        "engine_version": __version__,
        "config": session.config,
        "config_digest": session.config_digest,
        "content": content,
    }
    envelope["content_digest"] = _digest(
        {key: value for key, value in envelope.items() if key != "content_digest"}
    )
    return envelope


def parse_snapshot(
    snapshot: dict[str, object],
    config: dict[str, object] | None = None,
) -> tuple[dict[str, object], dict[str, _SymbolState], dict[str, tuple[str, str]]]:
    """Verify a snapshot document and return the restored session state.

    Version, configuration digest and content SHA-256 are verified before any
    state is built, and the whole session is assembled in locals that the
    caller adopts only after a successful return. Any failure raises
    :class:`SnapshotError` and leaves no partially recovered state behind.

    Returns ``(expected_config, symbols, events)``: the configuration the
    resumed session must run with, the per-security states and the global
    idempotency log.
    """
    if not isinstance(snapshot, dict):
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot must be a JSON object")
    if not set(snapshot) <= _ENVELOPE_KEYS_SNAPSHOT:
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot document has unknown fields")

    # A malformed caller configuration is a request error and is rejected
    # before any snapshot content (or the configuration comparison) is
    # consulted, so it never masquerades as a CONFIG_MISMATCH.
    _validate_config(dict(DEFAULT_CONFIG if config is None else config))

    version = snapshot.get("format_version")
    if version != FORMAT_VERSION:
        raise SnapshotError(
            SNAPSHOT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED,
            f"unsupported snapshot format version: {version!r}",
        )
    engine_version = snapshot.get("engine_version")
    if not isinstance(engine_version, str) or engine_version == "":
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot engine_version is malformed")

    expected_config = DEFAULT_CONFIG if config is None else config
    snapshot_config = snapshot.get("config")
    if snapshot_config != expected_config:
        raise SnapshotError(CONFIG_MISMATCH, "snapshot configuration does not match")
    if snapshot.get("config_digest") != _digest(expected_config):
        raise SnapshotError(CONFIG_MISMATCH, "snapshot configuration digest does not match")

    stored_digest = snapshot.get("content_digest")
    actual_digest = _digest(
        {key: value for key, value in snapshot.items() if key != "content_digest"}
    )
    if not isinstance(stored_digest, str) or stored_digest != actual_digest:
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot content digest mismatch")

    content = snapshot.get("content")
    if (
        not isinstance(content, dict)
        or set(content) != _CONTENT_KEYS
        or not isinstance(content.get("symbols"), list)
        or not isinstance(content.get("events"), list)
    ):
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot content is malformed")

    # The resumed session runs with the caller's configuration; a non-object
    # configuration is a request error, exactly as the session constructor
    # would raise before any snapshot content is adopted.
    if not isinstance(expected_config, dict):
        raise TypeError("config must be a JSON object or None")

    # Build the whole session in locals first; the caller commits it to the
    # session object only after every component parsed successfully.
    config_price_limits = {
        symbol: (bounds["lower"], bounds["upper"])
        for symbol, bounds in (expected_config.get("price_limits") or {}).items()
    }
    symbols: dict[str, _SymbolState] = {}
    events: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    for entry in content["symbols"]:
        if not (
            isinstance(entry, dict)
            and set(entry) == {"symbol", "state"}
            and isinstance(entry.get("symbol"), str)
            and isinstance(entry.get("state"), dict)
        ):
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot symbol entry is malformed")
        symbol = entry["symbol"]
        if symbol in symbols:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"duplicate symbol in snapshot: {symbol}")
        try:
            symbols[symbol] = _engine_from_json(
                entry["state"], config_price_limits.get(symbol)
            )
        except (KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"snapshot state for {symbol} is malformed") from exc
    for entry in content.get("events", []):
        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"event_id", "symbol", "content"}:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot event log is malformed")
        event_id = entry.get("event_id")
        symbol = entry.get("symbol")
        text = entry.get("content")
        if not isinstance(event_id, str) or not isinstance(symbol, str) or not isinstance(text, str):
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot event log entry is malformed")
        if symbol not in symbols:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"event {event_id} references unknown symbol")
        if event_id in events:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"duplicate event id in snapshot: {event_id}")
        events[event_id] = (symbol, text)

    # The global event log and the per-symbol event logs must describe exactly
    # the same accepted events, with identical normalized content.
    logged_per_symbol: dict[str, int] = {}
    for symbol, text in events.values():
        logged_per_symbol[symbol] = logged_per_symbol.get(symbol, 0) + 1
    for symbol, symbol_state in symbols.items():
        for event_id, text in symbol_state.seen.items():
            if events.get(event_id) != (symbol, text):
                raise SnapshotError(
                    SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT,
                    f"event {event_id} disagrees between global and symbol log",
                )
        if logged_per_symbol.get(symbol, 0) != len(symbol_state.seen):
            raise SnapshotError(
                SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT,
                f"event log counts disagree for symbol {symbol}",
            )

    return expected_config, symbols, events

"""Deterministic regression tests for segmentation-invariant multi-symbol replay.
